about: Curated dictionary of feared objects and situations used by src/lib/follow-up/triggers.ts. Objects are matched only after a fear, panic or avoidance cue ("afraid of X", "panic around X", "avoids X"). Terms are normalized and lightly stemmed like the symptom matcher, so regular plurals match; irregular forms are listed. `symptomId` names the phobia-type symptom of the lexicon an object belongs to (dogs: fear of animals), offered as a tap-to-add feature. Ids and categories are curated codes; the matched words stay on the device.

animal.label: Animals or insects
animal.clinicianNote: Fear centered on an animal or insect. Ask what happens when the animal is around, what the client does to keep away from it and what that costs day to day, and how real the risk is where they live. A bite or attack also calls for trauma questions.

natural-environment.label: Heights, storms, water or darkness
natural-environment.clinicianNote: Fear of heights, storms, water, darkness or similar settings. Check avoidance, how much daily life narrows around it, and whether a real current danger (for example, living in a storm-prone area after a disaster) makes the fear proportionate.

blood-injection-injury.label: Needles, blood, injury or medical care
blood-injection-injury.clinicianNote: Fear of needles, blood, injury or medical and dental care. Ask about fainting: this fear often brings a drop in heart rate and blood pressure after the first surge, which changes exposure planning (applied tension) and is worth telling medical staff. Check whether needed care is being delayed.

situational.label: Flying, enclosed spaces, driving or transport
situational.clinicianNote: Fear of flying, enclosed spaces, elevators, bridges, tunnels, driving, crowds or public transport. Ask whether the fear is about the situation itself (a crash, being shut in) or about not being able to get out or get help if panic strikes, across several kinds of places; the second points toward agoraphobia.

choking-vomiting.label: Choking, swallowing or vomiting
choking-vomiting.clinicianNote: Fear of choking, swallowing or vomiting. Make sure a swallowing or digestive problem has been checked, and ask about eating and weight: marked food restriction calls for a medical review.

social.label: Being watched, judged or embarrassed
social.clinicianNote: Fear of being watched, judged or embarrassed. Clarify whether the worry is about other people's evaluation (social anxiety) rather than about panic symptoms or escape (agoraphobia), and whether it covers many social situations or only performing.

contamination.label: Germs, dirt or contamination
contamination.clinicianNote: Fear of germs, dirt or contamination. Ask about repeated washing, cleaning or avoidance routines and the time they take; unwanted contamination thoughts followed by rituals point toward OCD.

trauma-reminder.label: Reminders of a frightening event
trauma-reminder.clinicianNote: The fear is tied to a frightening event (for example "since the attack" or "since the accident"). Ask what happened, when, and whether the client relives it; pace trauma questions, and offer safety questions.

health.label: Dying, heart attack or serious illness
health.clinicianNote: Fear of dying, a heart attack or a serious illness. Clarify whether it comes mainly during panic surges, is a steady fear of being or becoming seriously ill that reassurance settles only briefly (health anxiety), or centers on body symptoms that are clearly there, and make sure a medical review has been offered.
